channel.title: The College Fix - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The College Fix (thecollegefix.com)

item.title: Students don’t have attention span for whole films anymore: professors
item.description: Some film professors report that students now struggle to watch entire films, attributing this decline in attention span to excessive technology use.

item.title: Women’s & gender studies professor: Renee Good killed b/c she ‘knew white silence is violence’
item.description: Judy Rohrer criticizes white silence as violence in her response to Renee Good's death, claiming Good's actions against ICE represented a refusal to conform to societal norms. Rohrer likens this struggle to the civil rights movement, emphasizing the need for white individuals to actively oppose racism and support marginalized communities.

item.title: After huge snowstorm Penn climate scientists warn about … global warming
item.description: The recent significant snowstorm in the northeastern U.S. highlights the complex relationship between extreme weather and climate change. Professor Michael Mann warns that while such storms may occur, they indicate the impact of human-caused warming, emphasizing the need for decarbonization to prevent further climate extremes. Future storms are expected to worsen without significant action.

item.title: Professor: Alex Pretti’s death part of Trump’s ‘violent attack’ on illegal immigration in ‘minority’ cities
item.description: Professor Mark Shanahan argues the killing of Alex Pretti by ICE is tied to Trump's aggressive immigration stance, which he describes as a "violent attack" on minority communities. He claims Trump's use of federal agents relates to historical concerns from the founding fathers about authority and civil rights, suggesting a need for de-escalation.

item.title: Despite DEI bans, some public universities maintain DEI requirements, research finds
item.description: In total, diversity requirements, whether embedded in general education courses or as stand-alone graduation mandates, were found at universities within nearly a dozen states with DEI bans on the books, the report states.

item.title: Anti-Israel activists disrupt sympathetic liberal speaker at Sarah Lawrence College
item.description: At Sarah Lawrence College, anti-Israel activists disrupted a talk by liberal Ezra Klein, labeling him a "Nazi" despite his criticism of Israel. The event, titled "Building Bridges," aimed for dialogue, but protesters aggressively shouted accusations and chants, highlighting a lack of tolerance for opposing views on campus, according to observers.

item.title: Still no proof Indiana’s pro-life law hurt IU’s OB/GYN program
item.description: A pro-abortion professor said the state's protections for babies would harm med school recruitment. There is still no evidence to support her claim.

item.title: Are books trendy again? Gen Z is buying more paperbacks, starting campus reading clubs
item.description: Gen Z is buying more print books than Millennials, and some are starting book clubs on their campuses. The University of Miami also recently reported a resurgence in reading books for pleasure.

item.title: Judge tosses case claiming Northwestern Law discriminated against white men
item.description: Despite the loss in court, Northwestern University in December agreed to pay $75 million to resolve a federal anti-discrimination probe. As part of the settlement, the university agreed to end all affirmative action policies.

item.title: Texas A&M ends women’s and gender studies degrees
item.description: 'The decision reflected both the requirements of System policies and limited student interest in the program based on enrollment over the past several years.'
